thread.title: SPY Displaying A Holding Pattern, Here's How To Play It - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)

author: Todd Akin
title: SPY Displaying A Holding Pattern, Here's How To Play It - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)
text:
The overall market is showing strong resiliency as of late. Despite melting up to the $290 area earlier in 2018, the S&P 500 ( SPY ) has been holding up well, consolidating in an upward range.
To be sure, some indicators are currently flashing warning signs, such as interest rates rising, gas prices creeping higher, geopolitical instability with Iran and China escalating, SPY being overbought on a max time frame, and the VIX Volatility Index being low (Admittedly, there have been worse problems for investors to deal with).
Regardless of the negatives, the market needs to climb a wall of worry, anyway, in order to be healthy. Since the S&P 500 has averaged almost a 10% gain since inception, which is why it is the benchmark to beat, investors must buy the pullbacks, even if we need excuses like "Brexit" for buying opportunities along the way.
Well, the market has given investors a nice pullback from $290 to $250-260, but many stocks are still elevated near all-time highs, like tech giants Apple ( AAPL ) and Facebook ( FB ), while others, like bellwether energy players Exxon ( XOM ) and Halliburton ( HAL ), are still vastly underappreciated.
In addition to stock multiples being mixed, market indicators being neutral, stated above, makes for a tough environment to get aggressive on in SPY. However, there are ways to play the current scenario that the overall market is presenting to us, especially with leverage, which will be discussed further below.
Technicals on a One-Year SPY Chart Flashing Bullish The S&P 500 is above all moving averages, churning up along the 200-day moving average (black line), and seems to want to find support between the $250-260 trading range. SPY's candlesticks have also hammered on the 200-day moving average, adding further conviction to the $250-260 support area.
Source: E*Trade
SPY is also not overbought yet, which indicates that there is room to move higher from the current $270 level, up to potentially $280, where the next area of resistance lies. The RSI for SPY has stayed overbought in the past, so $280 doesn't have to be the top, since there isn't resistance again until $290 (the all-time highs).
SPY Technicals For Max Time Frame Overbought, Bearish Let's look at a max time frame of the market in order to get a more complete perspective. As one can see, SPY has been in a relatively narrow range from about $100 to $150 for about 20 years (1998-2017).
People's 401(k)s on average were plagued during that entire time, as the market saw one crash after another. Buy and hold seemed dead since most people were right back to where they started in 2016-2017 from the 08' crash.
Source: E*Trade
Thankfully, the S&P 500 finally broke out of that 20-year range with the Trump inauguration; Brexit was the last dip before the train left the station from the $200 area, all the way up to almost $300 ($290, so almost a 50% move up for SPY). With that said, SPY's RSI is still overbought on a max time frame, even with a recent 15% pullback from the highs. Overbought can mean overheated, as well as being a sign of strength, hence the mixed signal.
So, being that SPY has found support at the $250 levels recently implies that there is only about 20% downside risk to this market should we fall back to the old $200 breakout point. With an economy that's vastly improved from 2008, GDP growing under Trump, and BRIC countries booming (Brazil, Russia, India, and China), to name a few, it seems unlikely that the market would revisit the previous, agonizing 20-year range in which it toiled in, even if the market is overbought on a max time frame chart.
I spoke with some retirees on a cruise this year about the market, and most hadn't taken any profits. With how much their account has grown since the Trump breakout, they would be devastated by a crash, at their age.
"When the VIX is Low, It's Time to Go" I must mention that the VIX Volatility Index is also getting alarmingly low, which usually implies investor complacency and a lack of fear. I already mentioned that we need a wall of worry to climb, though. It is almost as if investors need to be more scared and panic in order for the proper buying opportunities to arise. In the past, every spike in the VIX has led to an instantaneous drop in the market (that should have been bought).
Source: E*Trade
It should also be noted though that the VIX can remain low while the market creeps higher. From last June to January 2018, the VIX remained relatively low while SPY exploded. When the economy is truly growing, a low VIX can work because there is no real fear for an actual good reason. Nonetheless, the VIX indicator must be taken seriously because when it spikes, SPY drops almost 100% of the time, historically.
Ways to Play the S&P 500 in a Cautiously Optimistic Scenario To me, if 20% down from these levels on SPY is all that I have to worry about, since revisiting the previous range under Trump seems unlikely, then I should think about getting more aggressive at these levels, and since institutional investors can be anticipatory of historical support and would probably step in and buy before those support levels, perhaps a 20% dip from here is even too lofty a target.
If SPY, indeed, falls back to $200 level from $250, the $200 area of old resistance (breakout point) should act as new support, and I would get extremely aggressive there. Since we are not there yet, the current landscape of a market that's had a big run, but yet is also too cheap to sell (mixed signals), requires a conservative money management strategy at the moment until volatility increases and buying opportunities present themselves again.
Leverage with Money Management? SPY offers an unmatched investment vehicle for investors with deep pockets. On a million dollar investment, for example, a 10% gain makes a nice dent in the portfolio. However, investors with, let's say, only a couple of thousand to play with might want more leverage in Ultra ProShares ( UPRO ).
UPRO precisely mimics the S&P 500, with triple leverage exposure, and has never let me down in the past, as far as execution or liquidity issue goes. However, investors with deeper pockets may want to be aware of the bid/ask spreads when placing an order. Again, I've never had an issue, and I've been in UPRO since its inception.
Source: E*Trade
The way to play the S&P 500 can be either through SPY or leveraged with vehicles like UPRO. But no matter which vehicle an investor chooses, the trick lies in money management and position size. Since the market is giving such mixed signals, and there is no such thing as a crystal ball, disciplined buy-points with proper position sizes are the only sure bet for long-term success.
Here is a working model for SPY position sizes, for example, given the generally neutral scenario we are presented with. If an investor has one million in their portfolio, roughly 40-60% of their money should then be invested in SPY now, and the other half left in cash, prudently ready to buy the dip.
If an investor chooses UPRO over SPY, then divide the position size by three, since it is leveraged times three. This is the strategy I currently use, which allows me to keep more spare cash, and affords me the ability to invest in other big names at the moment, such as these frac sand players.
Conclusion Since the environment SPY is currently operating in is essentially neutral, presenting mixed signals to investors, then their position sizes should be neutral, or half of their portfolio. If SPY breaks below the $250-260 level, which seems unlikely but not impossible by any means, THEN investors can get aggressive and deploy their dry powder at the $200 level, which should act as strong support for reasons listed above.
If SPY goes up 10% for the year, with only half of your one million invested, you still make $50,000. That's enough to change one's lifestyle. With UPRO, you could get the same leverage, for only a fraction of the cost, and still have cash left to play other opportunities (as seen by my portfolio below, albeit on a smaller scale). Conversely, if the market drops, you can now be ready to take advantage. Being half invested at these levels, or a quarter invested with UPRO, allows good participation to the upside, while having options to play the downside.
If I had to make a prediction, I would say the market stays rangebound for the year, churning higher in this channel, bringing the 200-day moving average up along with it. This coiling move could eventually create a springboard to push the S&P 500 past all-time highs.
But, if I had a crystal ball, I wouldn't be writing this article. I'd be on a mansion somewhere in space. Position size management, with UPRO, can even be more effective than SPY. If one invests all of their money in SPY, then there is no cash to buy the dip and really build wealth. Plus, you still get hurt pretty bad during a downturn. UPRO, conversely, allows you to receive the same gain as SPY, yet gives you the ability to buy the pullback (while taking advantage of other trades).
So, in other words, money management through the highest-quality investment vehicle in UPRO, if you prefer leverage, which averages a 10% (x3) return a year, will always be a win-win strategy that maximizes your cash. This strategy will work, as long as investors use money management techniques properly and stick to the strategic, long-term buy points discussed above.
Disclosure: I am/we are long UPRO.
